seo.title: Macro & Market Advisory | DNH
seo.description: Understand how inflation, currencies, liquidity, policy and market conditions affect assets, businesses and financial decisions.

sections.heading: Macro & Market Advisory: from economic change to financial decisions
paragraphs: Inflation, exchange rates, financing costs and market conditions do not mean the same thing for everyone. What matters is how they affect your assets, business and decisions.
Drawing on Dr Nasim Mohammadhassani’s specialist approach, DNH examines those effects and the options and risks connected with your decision.

media.alt: A conceptual macroeconomic and market analysis

sections.heading: One economic change does not have the same implications for everyone
paragraphs: Higher inflation, currency movements or changing financing conditions may affect an investor, family or business differently.
A decision needs to reflect how those changes interact with the actual financial position and objectives.

items.title: Purchasing power and capital value
items.description: Inflation can affect costs, real asset values and financial objectives.

items.title: Financing cost
items.description: Rates and credit conditions can alter both the cost and availability of funding.

items.title: Liquidity and access to capital
items.description: Economic conditions may affect asset sales or access to financial resources.

items.title: Risk and market conditions
items.description: Economic change can alter the relative risk and attractiveness of financial options.

sections.heading: Economic analysis is valuable when it relates to your decision
paragraphs: DNH Macro & Market Advisory goes beyond reviewing news and indicators.
It examines the variables relevant to your issue and connects them with financial conditions, options and possible implications.

items.title: Understand the economic environment
items.description: Review trends and variables that may affect the financial issue.

items.title: Analyse economic effects
items.description: Connect market changes with assets, liquidity, costs or business activity.

items.title: Examine strategic implications
items.description: Clarify risks, assumptions and questions requiring attention before a decision.

sections.closing: The DNH Intelligence Desk provides a general view of the environment; this advisory service applies the relevant information to a specific client issue.

sections.heading: Who can benefit from this service?
sections.intro: Where a financial decision is exposed to economic or market change, understanding the implications can support a more rigorous review of the options.

items.title: Investors and asset owners
items.description: Understand how inflation, currencies and markets affect capital structure, liquidity and asset risk.

items.title: Managers and business owners
items.description: Assess how economic conditions affect costs and cash flow before expansion, financing or allocation decisions.

items.title: Individuals and families
items.description: Review the implications of inflation, lower purchasing power or economic change for future goals.

sections.heading: Which economic variables affect your decision?
sections.intro: Not every indicator matters equally to every decision. The scope depends on the issue, market, geography and availability of reliable information.

items.title: Inflation and purchasing power
items.description: Effects on real capital value, costs and objectives.

items.title: Exchange rates
items.description: Effects on assets, obligations, income and costs.

items.title: Financial rates and funding
items.description: Changes in financing cost and access.

items.title: Liquidity and market conditions
items.description: Time, cost and constraints involved in trading or realising an asset.

items.title: Economic policy
items.description: Implications of monetary, fiscal and relevant regulatory changes.

items.title: Global markets and risks
items.description: Links between international developments, Iran’s economy and relevant markets.

sections.closing: The aim is not to review every indicator, but to identify the variables that matter most to the issue.

sections.heading: How can one economic change affect a business decision?
paragraphs: Consider a company planning an expansion while questioning how higher financing costs might affect the investment programme.
The effect pathway can be reviewed to clarify the issue.

sections.heading: A financial decision should not be based on one market alone
paragraphs: Currencies, equities, gold, property and financing conditions can share common economic drivers.
Considering those links prevents the implications from being viewed through only one asset or indicator.

items.title: Common risk drivers
items.description: One economic change may affect several assets or markets at once.

items.title: Changing liquidity
items.description: Tighter liquidity may affect trading and access to resources.

items.title: Changing relative appeal
items.description: Conditions can alter perceptions of the risk and return of different options.

items.title: Global developments and Iran
items.description: International change may affect currencies, costs and domestic markets.

sections.closing: Understanding cross-market links helps reveal hidden risks and wider decision implications.

sections.heading: If economic conditions change, what options remain?
sections.intro: A scenario is not a certain forecast. It helps identify which assumptions or parts of a decision could be affected by economic change.

items.title: Higher-than-expected inflation
items.description: How would higher costs affect purchasing power, liquidity and plans?

items.title: Exchange-rate volatility
items.description: How might currency movements affect asset values, income or obligations?

items.title: Liquidity constraints
items.description: Which decisions need review if access to resources becomes more difficult?

items.title: Policy change
items.description: Which assumptions need revisiting if regulation or financing conditions change?

sections.closing: The aim is greater preparedness for different conditions—not precise prediction of market outcomes.

sections.heading: From defining the issue to examining strategic implications
sections.intro: DNH links Data Intelligence, Navigation Strategy and Horizon Architecture to the client’s specific issue.

items.title: Define the analysis

sections.note: The sequence data → analysis → insight → scenario → decision explains how the three DNH pillars work together; it is not a separate framework.

sections.heading: What becomes clearer for the decision after the review?
paragraphs: Outputs depend on the issue, agreed scope and reliable information available.
The purpose is a decision-useful view of economic conditions and their potential implications.

sections.note: This advisory does not issue trading signals, predict prices with certainty, guarantee returns or manage capital. Output format and detail are agreed before specialist work begins.

sections.heading: How are economic changes affecting your financial decision?
paragraphs: If you face an important decision involving investment, assets, financing or business expansion, understanding the economic setting can support a more rigorous review.
DNH’s initial assessment clarifies the issue so that an appropriate specialist scope can be defined where suitable.
sections.closing: You do not need to provide confidential documents or complete asset details at the initial stage.
